details.description: Amazon Polly Standard is the original text-to-speech engine in AWS's Amazon Polly service, using concatenative synthesis that joins phonemes of recorded human speech into audio. It is one of four Polly voice engines, alongside Neural, Long-Form and Generative, which AWS documents as producing more natural, human-like speech than Standard. AWS currently offers 60 Standard voices (40 female, 20 male) across 29 languages and language variants, each usable for real-time or asynchronous synthesis with SSML markup and Polly speech marks.
advantages: Offers 60 voices (40 female, 20 male) across 29 languages and language variants, per AWS's Standard voices documentation.
AWS describes the concatenative synthesis it uses as producing 'very natural-sounding synthesized speech' by joining phonemes of recorded human speech.
Supports real-time and asynchronous synthesis operations, all Polly speech marks, and most SSML tags.
Lets users choose from multiple sampling rates (22 kHz default) and output audio as MP3, OGG Vorbis, or raw PCM.
disadvantages: AWS says concatenative synthesis has an inherent ceiling: 'the inevitable variations in speech and the techniques used to segment the waveforms limits the quality of speech' compared with its Neural, Long-Form and Generative engines.
Many newer Polly voices are Neural-, Long-Form- or Generative-only and are not offered on the Standard engine, per AWS's available voices table.
use_cases: Adding spoken narration to websites, RSS feeds, or videos for a global audience.
Powering IVR prompts and automated voice-response systems for customer engagement.
Creating voiceovers for animations, games, and other media directly from scripts, with SSML control over phrasing.
Making mobile and IoT applications voice-enabled.

sources.title: AI Voice Generator and Text-to-Speech Tool - Amazon Polly - AWS

notes: aws_polly/standard is Amazon Polly's Standard voice engine (concatenative synthesis), distinct from Polly's Neural, Long-Form and Generative engines. Confirmed current on AWS's docs as of 2026-09-25: the Standard engine has no deprecation notice and remains listed alongside the other three engines with full voice/region tables. No accuracy-style benchmark scores are published by AWS for any Polly engine, so evaluations is empty. Catalog facts (endpoints, audio_output/text_input modality) do not conflict with anything found.
